analysis.title: Inside Commodities, November 4, 2026
key_insights: Gulf seaborne oil exports (crude, condensate, products, ex-LPG) averaged 17.1M bpd in October per Vortexa, down from 18.9M bpd in September and about three-quarters of pre-war levels. Vortexa and Kpler both say October is more likely to be revised up than down because tankers switch off tracking near Hormuz.
Crude and condensate exports averaged 14.0M bpd in October (about 86% of pre-war levels). Refined product exports averaged 3.1M bpd, just over half of normal volumes.

Attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz reached a record in October. Saudi exports were steady versus September, the UAE had the largest decline, and Iraq, Oman and Kuwait all exported less. Iran is excluded because it is not exporting under the US blockade.

Oil services executives at an Abu Dhabi conference say Iran war costs are eating into Middle East contract margins: logistics costs up as much as threefold, fuel costs doubled, labour costs up 30-40% (Maire CEO). Saipem says it has been sitting outside Hormuz for months. NESR says it is absorbing the costs.

India's October palm oil imports rose 6% m/m to 866,000 t (highest since August 2025) and soyoil imports hit a record 653,000 t. Total edible oil imports rose 13% to 1.74M t, a more than two-year high. Dealers expect palm imports to stay elevated in November because palm trades at a discount to rival oils. This could support palm oil futures by curbing stock growth in Indonesia and Malaysia.

India's E20 ethanol blending is likely to fall to 15-17% this supply year from 20% after monsoon rainfall came in nearly 13% below normal. Corn and sugar rose about 40% to record highs, rice rose 20%, and September retail food inflation was 7.74% versus 5.97% in August. India's corn output could fall as much as 15% from last year's record 55M t.

India directed oil companies not to buy ethanol made from sugar-based feedstocks and cut the corn-based ethanol purchase price to 68.86 rupees/litre from 71.86. Distillers with about 20B litres/year of capacity face overcapacity. E20 has saved about 2T rupees ($21.1B) in oil import costs since 2014, so lower blending raises India's reliance on imported crude.

The World Gold Council expects India's 2026 gold demand to fall to about 650 t, a six-year low. September-quarter demand fell 29% y/y to 162.5 t, with jewellery down 20% and investment down 40%. Festival and wedding demand may help the December quarter, but high prices and a weak rural economy cap it.

Gold fell below $4,000/oz on Friday, its lowest in a year, during an equity selloff driven by AI-boom concerns. Gold has lost about a quarter of its value since the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28 and is down 9% year to date, the worst of 14 asset classes in BofA's list. It trades about 10% below its 200-day moving average, the most oversold in BofA's ranking.

Gold's three-month correlation with the S&P 500 is 0.48 and its one-month correlation is 0.69 (Standard Chartered). StanChart says gold's role as a source of cash is likely to outweigh its safe-haven role in the short term. Q3 central bank gold purchases rose 42% to 321 t, the most since Q4 2024, led by Poland and China.

Germany entered winter with record-low gas storage of 61.05% as of November 2, versus a 74.56% EU average and Germany's roughly 70% target. EU gas prices are at a four-year high. Raiffeisen's Aaron Alber sees German storage ending winter at 20-25% instead of 30-40%.

QatarEnergy signed a 20-year deal for 3 mtpa of US LNG from Woodside's Louisiana facilities and a deal for up to 4 mtpa from Cheniere through 2054. Deliveries start in 2030-2031, making Qatar the largest buyer of US LNG. Reuters columnist Bousso reads this as Qatar hedging Hormuz risk and as a shift in energy market power toward the US.

An Iranian missile in March damaged two of QatarEnergy's 14 LNG trains at Ras Laffan, removing about 17% of export capacity. QatarEnergy puts the loss at about $20B a year, with repairs taking about three years. Qatari LNG costs about $3-5/MMBtu, roughly half of many US projects.
IEA expects about 300 bcm of new global LNG export capacity in 2025-2030, about 50% more supply, with more than half from the US and about a quarter from Qatar.

Two French vessels will load more than 60,000 t of wheat each for Saudi Arabia, the first French bulk wheat shipments there since 2020. South Korea's CAPI bought up to 67,000 t of corn in a tender at about $264.69/t c&f for 52,350 t, with the rest at a premium of 211.59 US cents/bu over CH27.

sector_views.rationale: Executives report logistics, fuel and labour cost increases on Middle East contracts that are squeezing margins, and the companies are absorbing the costs.
Gold is oversold versus its 200-day moving average, but StanChart expects liquidity needs to outweigh safe-haven demand in the near term.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 5.97% in August after El Niño crop damage, which pushes the government to put food ahead of ethanol.
Down from 18.9M bpd in September and likely to be revised up. Still about three-quarters of pre-war flows.

macro_indicators.indicator: Kpler crude and condensate flows through Hormuz, Red Sea and Gulf of Oman

macro_indicators.interpretation: Below the 74.56% EU average and Germany's roughly 70% target, which leaves little buffer for a cold winter.
WGC expects a six-year low on high prices and a weak rural economy.
Lowest in a year despite risk-off conditions.
Below the 20% target, leaving India more dependent on imported crude.

crypto_views: Persistent bitcoin weakness and last week's $6.3B cyberattack at Binance, potentially the largest financial heist, have given gold no support.
risk_factors: Tanker tracking signals are switched off near Hormuz, so Gulf export data is revised up later.
Hormuz shipping attacks and insurance costs are raising project costs and energy prices.
Record-low German gas storage heading into winter, with gas prices at a four-year high.
Equity-market losses could force liquidity selling in gold.
A weak monsoon could further cut Indian ethanol feedstocks, rural incomes and gold demand.
Food inflation is politically sensitive ahead of early 2027 Indian state elections.
vol_and_positioning: Gold one-week realized volatility reached 90% when it peaked at $5,595/oz last January.
Gold trades about 10% below its 200-day moving average, about five times more oversold than government bonds on that measure (BofA).
Gold's correlation with the S&P 500 is positive and strengthening: 0.48 over three months and 0.69 over one month (Standard Chartered).
geopolitical: US-Iran war in its ninth month (began February 28 with US and Israeli attacks), with attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz at a record in October.
US blockade has stopped Iranian oil exports.
Washington and Tehran continue to dispute the future of the Strait of Hormuz.
Saudi Arabia and the UAE are expanding pipelines that bypass Hormuz.
Iranian missile damage at Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG facility in March.
Germany rejected Italy's accusation that it under-filled gas storage to cut costs ahead of importer privatisation.
Last week's $6.3B cyberattack at crypto exchange Binance.

tension_points.bull_case: Gold is the most oversold asset class in BofA's ranking, about 10% below its 200-day moving average, and central bank buying rose 42% in Q3 to 321 t, so mean reversion could produce a bounce.
tension_points.bear_case: Gold's correlation with equities is positive and rising (0.48 three-month, 0.69 one-month). Standard Chartered says liquidity needs from equity losses are likely to make investors sell gold, and an IMF paper found bullion is not a reliable hedge.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further equity-market turbulence that triggers liquidity needs would keep gold under pressure and undercut the mean-reversion case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Gold's role as a liquidity provider and the need to generate cash are likely to overshadow its safe-haven role in the short term.

theme_stances.key_argument: Heightened Hormuz risks pulled Middle East seaborne oil exports back from recent post-war highs.
theme_stances.evidence: pulled back slightly from recent post-war highs on heightened risks in the Strait of Hormuz
